title: Cross-Strategy Production Reliability Gates
goal_statement: Start local/static/fixture cross-strategy production reliability gates after CR153 Event-Driven Strategy E2E first-wave closure.
scope_summary: CR154 passed Rule 41, CP0, CP1, CP2, CP3, CP4, CP5, CP6, CP7 and CP8.
CP7 passed with risk after QA-driven rework of Gate 1/2/4/5/6 fail-closed behavior.
CP8 DEC-CR154-CP8-001 accepted the five residual risk items and closed CR154 as READY_WITH_RISK.
No runtime, real data, broker, credential, feed, order, reconciliation, store/catalog/registry/publish or trading action is authorized.
approval_focus: CR154 CP2 approved local/static/fixture first-wave scope for cross-strategy production reliability gates and no-runtime/no-real-data boundary.
approve_effect: CR154 entered CP3 design only; no Story, LLD, source implementation, runtime, data, broker, credential, feed, order, reconciliation or publish action is authorized.
reject_effect: N/A after CP2 approval; future changes require CP3 review changes_requested or a new CR.
not_authorized_by_approve: feature store / label store / event store / model registry / prediction store writes
true release execution / production deployment / publish
decision_burden: none; DEC-CR154-CP8-001 accepted by user; no runtime, real data, broker, credential, feed, order, reconciliation, store/catalog/registry, publish or trading action is authorized.
remaining_risks: Fixture/static validation must not be represented as production reliability proof.
CP7 passed after QA-driven rework, but first-wave validation remains static/fixture-only.
New CR154 source and test files must be included in the final change set before commit or release.
CP6 story return path warnings remain non-blocking process hygiene.
Admission default policy could change historical CR151/CR152/CR153 caller behavior and must be explicitly gated.
Capacity/impact/reconciliation slots must not be mistaken for real TCA, broker reconciliation, runtime readiness or trading readiness.
Data-lake/NAS/provider/runtime candidates remain deferred and must not be silently pulled into CR154 first wave.
split_rationale: CR154 is cross-strategy because backtest traps, OOS governance, survivorship-free universe, capacity/impact, regime, attribution, reconciliation and default admission policy are shared by multifactor, ML and event-driven strategies.
why_not_merge_with_parent: Roadmap and remediation plan are planning artifacts; CR154 needs a formal CP2 scope baseline before design and implementation.
why_not_story_or_task: The change affects requirements, strategy admission semantics, validation gates, release blocking policy and cross-strategy architecture, so it requires formal CR and checkpoint flow.
user_goal_impact: Improves strategy framework reliability before any production data, runtime, paper/live or broker readiness is considered.

cp3_design_constraints.summary: Backtest trap gate must expose auditable statistical reliability artifacts for multiple-testing/FDR-BH/WRC-SPA/PBO-CSCV/DSR-deflation/trial-count/OOS/purge-embargo/survivorship/impact-capacity evidence, with n/a-with-reason for unavailable fields.
HLD / ADR must include UC / REQ -> Architecture traceability and decide whether CR154 reuses existing REQ anchors or later adds CR154-specific requirements.
HLD / ADR must define an admission default policy tier table covering opt-in, default-required, release-blocking, exceptions and rollback.
HLD / ADR must define how CR153 universe_pit_audit remains compatible while delegating or adapting to the CR154 PIT universe gate.
HLD / ADR must define impact_model_family as a controlled enum including square_root, almgren_chriss and gatheral, with custom or n/a-with-reason policy.
HLD / ADR must classify ML-only triple-barrier/meta-labeling and feature-importance methods as strategy-specific n/a for non-ML strategies and keep them outside CR154 cross-strategy release blockers.
